policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'brought them into subjection' is compatible with both the qere and ketiv forms and supplies no mapped textual note distinguishing them; retain the documented qere base fallback.
ASV's main wording 'to be tossed to and fro' distinguishes the ketiv reading לזועה; the note 'Or, a terror unto' is classed alternative_rendering and therefore does not decide the textual reading.
